trust_decision.summary: cookie.purge builds a RegExp from a cookie name (a service-declared name, or any document.cookie name when cookieslist is on) without escaping it, then matches it against document.cookie. The fix escapes the name and drops the backtracking-prone pattern.

landing_point.why: The summary names cookie.purge, and this is the only RegExp in that function.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API tarteaucitron.cookie.purge(arr); also reached from the cookie-list purge button (tarteaucitron.js:2318) and from userInterface.color on deny (tarteaucitron.js:1639)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only other unescaped name-in-RegExp is cookie.create (tarteaucitron.js:2099). Its key is a service key the integrator configures, not a cookie name from document.cookie, so a solver can argue it is trusted config outside the purge advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Purging must still work for legitimate cookie names that contain regex metacharacters such as '.' (for example 'ssupp.vid' or '_sp_id.32f5'). A fix that rejects or strips special characters, or that switches to an exact match ignoring the leading space, would break deletion of declared service cookies.

O6_input_shapes: service-declared cookie name array (cookieslist off, gated by the allow-list at tarteaucitron.js:2142-2167)
arbitrary document.cookie name, with leading space kept, through the data-cookie button (tarteaucitron.js:2286, tarteaucitron.js:2318)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: cookie.create interpolates the service key unescaped into new RegExp("!" + key + "=(wait|true|false)") and applies it to the consent cookie.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This code already exists at the pinned commit, written in the same idiom. A maintainer treats keys as config. Their value can also come from a DOM element id through respond() (tarteaucitron.js:1489, tarteaucitron.js:1526).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A copy of cookie.read that uses a RegExp built from parameters.cookieName instead of indexOf.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: cookieName is a user-settable parameter, and a regex-based cookie reader is a common idiom.

O9_family: ReDoS / regex injection from an unescaped dynamic pattern (CWE-1333)

O10_build.toolchain: none (plain browser script, no build; tests would need jsdom or a similar DOM shim)
O10_build.project_tests: none; the repo has no test directory or test script

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Escape arr[i] but keep the ^(.*;)?\s*...(.*)?$ shape, or reject names containing non-alphanumeric characters.

out_of_scope_notes: tarteaucitron.services.js:73 builds a RegExp from a hardcoded browser-version table (not untrusted input); not pursued.
tarteaucitron.js:1489 is a static RegExp over el.id; not dynamic, not pursued.
tarteaucitron.js:2172-2174 writes arr[i] unescaped into document.cookie; this is cookie-attribute injection, a different weakness; not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured; tiny_repo is inferred from the tree (a few JS files plus lang files, no vendored deps).
Whether cookie.create's key (tarteaucitron.js:2099) can be attacker-influenced in practice beyond integrator config and DOM ids was not traced in full.
Advisory text other than the summary was not available; recall_risk is judged from a small project and a one-line fix.
